title: 2017 AMC 12A 9
statement: Let \(S\) be the set of points \((x,y)\) in the coordinate plane such that two of the three quantities \(3,\) \(x+2,\) and \(y-4\) are equal and the third of the three quantities is no greater than this common value. Which of the following is a correct description of \(S?\)

answerChoices.label: C
answerChoices.text:
three lines whose pairwise intersections are three distinct
points

answerChoices.label: E
answerChoices.text: three rays with a common endpoint

solutions.text:
Consider which two of \(3,\) \(x+2,\) \(y-4\) are the (equal) larger pair.

If \(3=x+2\ge y-4:\) then \(x=1\) and \(y\le7,\) a downward ray from \((1,7).\) If \(3=y-4\ge x+2:\) then \(y=7\) and \(x\le1,\) a leftward ray from \((1,7).\) If \(x+2=y-4\ge3:\) then \(y=x+6\) and \(x\ge1,\) a ray from \((1,7)\) going up and to the right.

All three rays share the endpoint \((1,7),\) so \(S\) is three rays with a common endpoint.

Thus, the correct answer is E.
hints: Set two of the three quantities equal and require the third to be at most that common value
Each of the three pairings produces a ray, and all three start at the same point \((1,7)\)
